title: Restriction of a groupoid to an invariant open and transport of degree
statement: Let $U,R$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with maps $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ defining a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Let $W\subseteq U$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] satisfying $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$ as open subsets, and denote the common open subscheme by $V$. Write $j:W\hookrightarrow U$ and $k:V\hookrightarrow R$ for the inclusions. There are unique restrictions $s_W,t_W:V\to W$, $e_W:W\to V$, $i_W:V\to V$, and $c_W:V\times_{s_W,W,t_W}V\to V$ [def-pc-fibre-product] forming a groupoid scheme. They satisfy $j\circ s_W=s\circ k$, $j\circ t_W=t\circ k$, $k\circ e_W=e\circ j$, $k\circ i_W=i\circ k$, and $k\circ c_W=c\circ\lambda$, where $\lambda:V\times_{s_W,W,t_W}V\to R\times_{s,U,t}R$ is induced by $k$ on both factors. The map $i_W$ is an involutive isomorphism and $s_W\circ i_W=t_W$, so it identifies the morphisms $t_W$ and $s_W$ over $W$. For every integer $r\geq0$, if $s_W$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], then $t_W$ is finite locally free of degree $r$. The open $W$ may be empty; affineness and finite locally free hypotheses on the original $s,t$ are not required.

proof.text: By $V=s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$, both $s\circ k$ and $t\circ k$ have image in $W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to obtain unique $s_W,t_W:V\to W$ with $j s_W=s k$ and $j t_W=t k$. The inclusions $j$ and $k$ are monomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]; consequently equalities of maps into $W$ or $V$ can be checked after these inclusions.

source.place: Tag 03BC (definition-invariant-open), following paragraph; restriction maps in Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), expanded using Schemes Tags 01HI and 01L7

proof.text: The groupoid identities $s e=\mathrm{id}_U$ and $s i=t$ are part of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Thus $e(j(W))\subseteq s^{-1}(W)=V$ and $i(k(V))\subseteq s^{-1}(W)=V$, the latter because $t(k(V))\subseteq W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to obtain unique $e_W:W\to V$ and $i_W:V\to V$ satisfying $k e_W=e j$ and $k i_W=i k$. These are actual morphisms of schemes, not merely maps of underlying sets.

source.place: Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), omitted construction expanded; Tag 03BC following paragraph

proof.text: Put $P=V\times_{s_W,W,t_W}V$, with projections $p_0,p_1$. Since $s k p_0=j s_Wp_0=j t_Wp_1=t k p_1$, [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the unique map $\lambda:P\to R\times_{s,U,t}R$ with projections $k p_0,k p_1$. The identity $s c=s\operatorname{pr}_1$ of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] implies $s c\lambda=s k p_1=j s_Wp_1$. Hence $c\lambda$ has image in $V=s^{-1}(W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] it factors uniquely as $k c_W$, defining $c_W:P\to V$ and the required compatibility with composition.

source.place: Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), omitted construction of composition expanded; Tag 03BC following paragraph

proof.text: For each test scheme $H$, the injective maps $W(H)\to U(H)$ and $V(H)\to R(H)$ identify the restricted operations with the original ones. Indeed this follows from the five commuting equations just proved and the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product]. The equations $s_We_W=t_We_W=\mathrm{id}_W$, $s_Wi_W=t_W$, $t_Wi_W=s_W$, $s_Wc_W=s_Wp_1$ and $t_Wc_W=t_Wp_0$ follow by composing with $j$, using the corresponding identities of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], and cancelling $j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. For $a,b,d\in V(H)$ with matching endpoints, composing the two restricted unit equations, the two inverse equations, and $c_W(c_W(a,b),d)=c_W(a,c_W(b,d))$ with $k$ gives exactly the original equations in $R(H)$. Cancel $k$ to obtain all of them. Naturality in $H$ is precomposition of scheme morphisms. Thus [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] applies. Uniqueness of all five maps was already supplied by their factorizations.

source.place: Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), omitted verification of groupoid laws expanded

proof.text: Apply the groupoid laws from [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] directly to the restricted groupoid. For an arrow a, associativity for (i(i(a)), i(a), a), the two inverse equations, and the two unit equations give i(i(a)) = a: its left-associated composite is a and its right-associated composite is i(i(a)). In Lean take the test scheme V and the universal arrow id_V. This proves i_W squared is id_V without cancelling an inclusion. Hence i_W is its own inverse as a scheme isomorphism. The restricted inverse-source law gives i_W followed by s_W equals t_W.

source.place: Tag 03BI (lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), final sentence: inverse identifies source and target

proof.text: Assume s_W is finite locally free of degree r, as defined in [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Rewrite t_W as i_W followed by s_W. Mathlib instances for [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] show that isomorphisms have each property and that each property is closed under composition. These provide the three fields of the finite locally free structure on t_W.

source.place: Tag 03BI (lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), final sentence, isomorphism transport expanded from the definitions

proof.text: For each w in W, apply the already proved source-library lemma AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fiberDegree_comp_left_of_isIso to i_W and s_W. It identifies the fibre degree of i_W followed by s_W with that of s_W; its proof is the pullback comparison from [def-pc-fibre-product] and the fibre-degree definition of [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The latter degree is r by hypothesis. This completes the degree-r structure on t_W. No point of W was chosen globally, so the construction and proof also cover the empty open.

source.place: Tag 03BI (lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), final sentence, fibre-degree comparison expanded

lean.statement: theorem IsGroupoidScheme.existsUnique_invariantOpen_restriction_degree {U R : Scheme.{u}} (s t : R ⟶ U) (e : U ⟶ R) (i : R ⟶ R) (c : pullback s t ⟶ R) (hG : IsGroupoidScheme s t e i c) (W : U.Opens) (hW : s ⁻¹ᵁ W = t ⁻¹ᵁ W) : ∃ (sW tW : (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ⟶ W.toScheme) (eW : W.toScheme ⟶ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme) (iW : (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ⟶ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme) (cW : pullback sW tW ⟶ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme) (hs : sW ≫ W.ι = (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ s) (ht : tW ≫ W.ι = (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ t), (∀ sW' : (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ⟶ W.toScheme, sW' ≫ W.ι = (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ s ↔ sW' = sW) ∧ (∀ tW' : (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ⟶ W.toScheme, tW' ≫ W.ι = (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ t ↔ tW' = tW) ∧ (∀ eW' : W.toScheme ⟶ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme, eW' ≫ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι = W.ι ≫ e ↔ eW' = eW) ∧ (∀ iW' : (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ⟶ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme, iW' ≫ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι = (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ i ↔ iW' = iW) ∧ (∀ cW' : pullback sW tW ⟶ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme, cW' ≫ (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι = pullback.map sW tW s t (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι W.ι hs ht ≫ c ↔ cW' = cW) ∧ IsGroupoidScheme sW tW eW iW cW ∧ IsIso iW ∧ iW ≫ iW = 𝟙 (s ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ∧ iW ≫ sW = tW ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, sW.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r → tW.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r
